biography.plain_text: David Mueller is an American airline entrepreneur who co-founded Comair in 1977 with financial backing from his father, Raymond. He led the Cincinnati-based carrier as it expanded regional air services and introduced passenger jets. The business became part of Delta Air Lines, and Mueller subsequently served as an adviser to Delta.

confidence.reason: Institutional and direct-report evidence establish the foundation, paternal support and jet strategy; the completed buyer filing and museum corroborate the subsequent relationship. Overall confidence is limited by the compound identity bridge.

long_biography.plain_text:
On Comair’s early flights, David Mueller handled baggage, sold tickets and took reservations as well as flying the aircraft. He had studied business at the University of Cincinnati, graduating in 1975. As the small operation grew, its staff recorded passengers’ bookings on cards kept in a recipe box.

Mueller also bred thoroughbred horses through Mueller Farms. Working with bloodstock specialists, he bought broodmares whose offspring went through the sales ring. One was Skybox, the dam of Stopshoppingmaria. After leaving his Northern Kentucky farm, he kept his remaining mares with John Stuart in Lexington.

confidence.reason: The detailed early-career report and specialist breeder coverage directly support each material claim, including the booking system and later location of the mares. The text uses historical tense and does not make him Stopshoppingmaria's later racing owner. Identity linkage caps the score.
